installSteps.text: Alternatively, download Frontline Zero — Free-to-Play Real-Time Strategy directly from the official site at https://www.frontlinezero.com/. Always download from the official source — third-party mirrors of free games are a common malware vector.

Run the downloaded installer and follow the prompts. If Windows SmartScreen warns about an unrecognised publisher, that is normal for open-source projects without a paid code-signing certificate — choose More info, then Run anyway.
Open the downloaded .dmg and drag the app into Applications. On first launch macOS may refuse to open it as unidentified — right-click the app and choose Open to approve it once.
Check your distribution's package manager first, which is usually the easiest route. Otherwise download the AppImage from the official site, mark it executable and run it.

Launch the game and look at the settings menu before your first session — resolution and control defaults are worth checking. Frontline Zero — Free-to-Play Real-Time Strategy needs roughly small of free disk space.

set.tagline: Hold the town for income, find eyes for your artillery, and move before the return fire.
set.description: Frontline Zero is a free browser RTS from 556 Games. Build a base, capture towns and oil fields, and field infantry, armor, drones and artillery. Train or skirmish against AI, then play 1v1 or 2v2 in the game's online rooms.

systemRequirements.min: A current JavaScript-capable browser and internet connection for online play. The developer publishes no numerical CPU, RAM, GPU or disk minimum.
systemRequirements.recommended: No recommended hardware tier is published. A desktop browser gives room for the command sidebar; the game also advertises phone and tablet browser play.

min.notes: Free browser game requiring JavaScript. Numerical CPU, RAM, GPU and storage minimums are not published by 556 Games.

recommended.notes: No recommended numerical tier is published. Use a current browser and a stable connection for online matches.

set.launcherInstall.note: Open the official browser game. No desktop installer is required. Steam and GOG desktop editions are listed as coming soon by the developer; they are not PlayBound download recipes.

qualityBar.verdict: A familiar base-building scramble with a modern problem: the gun that hits from far away can be found and hit back.

set.longDescription:
Frontline Zero brings an old RTS rhythm to a contemporary battlefield. Build a base, collect income and push through a tech tree, then send infantry, armor and aircraft toward the ground you need to hold. Towns and industrial sites pay for expansion; oil fields can run dry. The economy is readable in classic strategy terms, but the military decisions have a modern edge. Drones find targets, jammers interfere, and air defenses determine whether the sky belongs to anyone at all.

Artillery makes the sharpest point. Mortars, howitzers and rockets can strike well beyond the reach of the troops beneath them, but they need someone to see the target. Moving units can avoid shells, and enemy guns can hunt the battery that fired. A good shot is therefore only half a plan. The other half is leaving before the counterattack arrives. That loop gives a player an immediate reason to scout, relocate and pay attention to the map instead of building a neat base and watching numbers rise.

The developer sets skirmishes on maps based on real places in the Russia–Ukraine war. You can play Ukraine or Russia, alone against several AI difficulties or online with other players. The available formats are 1v1 and 2v2, with regional rooms and invitations for friends. Training chapters and a unit handbook give newcomers a route into its equipment and tech tree. Replays let you see where a plan held and where it fell apart. The people depicted are fictional, a distinction the developer makes explicitly.

The game is free to open in a modern browser on a computer, tablet or phone. Online multiplayer and AI skirmishes are part of that free version. A one-time Supporter purchase unlocks extras such as the map editor, personal community-map access, save/load in AI skirmish and a battle sandbox; it does not buy a combat advantage online. The developer lists Steam and GOG desktop releases as upcoming, so PlayBound should open the current browser game rather than pretending a native desktop file is ready to install.

Frontline Zero hosts its own online matches. No separately downloadable dedicated server or virtual-LAN setup is documented, and a PlayBound party has not been tested to join the same in-game room automatically. Touch play on a phone is also not evidence of a physical-controller layout. The developer has not published numerical hardware minimums, so a current JavaScript-capable browser is the honest starting requirement. What interests us is the tension between comfortable base building and equipment that punishes a static plan. The game remains a Draft candidate until the online join flow and the tactical feel are tested directly.
set.whyWePickedIt: A free browser RTS with actual 1v1 and 2v2 rooms is easy for friends to try, and its artillery, drones and counterfire give classic base building a distinctive set of decisions. We still need a hands-on multiplayer test before calling the PlayBound party path ready.
set.thatOneThing: Your artillery can hit across the map. So can the reply if you leave it in the same spot.

installSteps.text: Open frontlinezero.com in a modern browser with JavaScript enabled. The browser version is free and needs no local installer.
Use the six-part Training mode or start an AI skirmish to learn bases, income, scouting and artillery.
For online play, open the game's Multiplayer screen and create or join a regional 1v1 or 2v2 room. Use its own friend-invite flow; automatic PlayBound party handoff is not verified.

firstPlaySteps.text: Play a Training chapter, then take a nearby town for income before investing in a larger force.

multiplayerGamingSteps.text: Use Frontline Zero's online rooms and friend invitations for 1v1 or 2v2. Matchmaking is handled by the game, not a PlayBound-hosted dedicated server.
